chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who sleeps and does not see in his sleep that he had a wet dream, then he finds moisture in his garment and on his thigh. Is ghusl obligatory upon him? He said: "Yes."

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because the way to reconcile them is that when a garment that no one else shares with him in using is found to have semen on it, ghusl and the repetition of salat (prayer) are obligatory upon him if he had already prayed, since it is possible that he forgot the wet dream. But as for that in which someone else shares with him, it does not make ghusl obligatory upon him unless he becomes certain of the wet dream.

key_terms.الِاحْتِلَامَ: the occurrence of a wet dream
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the fluid found, referring here to seminal moisture

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory if someone finds semen on his clothes after sleep but does not remember a wet dream?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of ghusl when a person finds signs of janabah after sleep without remembering a wet dream. It distinguishes between finding semen on a garment used exclusively by the person and one shared with others, making certainty and probable attribution central to the legal ruling.
